The ending of the story feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned. Throughout the narrative, Daniel is haunted by the unexamined remnants of his past marriage, symbolized by the recurring dream of the empty flat. By gradually opening up to Isabel and engaging in a "mutual inventory" of their pasts, the dream begins to lose its hold on him. The discovery of the old narrowboat keys serves as a bridge between his past regrets and his present life, prompting the canoe trip with Isabel. 

The conclusion ties up the central conflict—Daniel realizes the dreams have stopped because his mind was simply "locking up" that old life—and brings the thematic elements full circle. By repeating the phrase "We should do this every year" to Isabel, Daniel reclaims a failed promise from his past and transforms it into a meaningful "offering" in his current relationship, providing a deeply satisfying sense of closure and emotional resolution.
